name: Salem
story_so_far: After the shipwreck, I washed up with Reem, Khalid, Noura, and Faisal. Faisal died of hunger and exhaustion, a loss that haunts me. I was our provider until an ankle injury left me immobile. As supplies vanished, the group fractured; Reem became selfish, attempting to trade wood for food, while Khalid struggled to survive. Eventually, the hunger took them both. Reem and Khalid died from exhaustion and starvation on Day 12. Now, only Noura and I remain. I am physically broken and starving, left with 6 units of wood and the crushing guilt of my inability to help Noura. She is our only hope, and I feel utterly useless as I watch her face the jungle alone to keep us alive.

Reem.note: She died trying to prioritize herself over the group, showing how hunger can strip away humanity.

Khalid.note: I feel a profound sense of failure for not being able to keep my promise to help him survive.

Noura.note: She is my sole companion and the only reason I am still breathing, though I fear her exhaustion will take her too.

Faisal.note: His death was the first tragedy that set this cycle of loss in motion.

plans: I will wait by the camp for Noura's return and try to conserve every bit of energy I have left, hoping she brings enough food to stabilize us.

diary.text: Today was exhausting, but I'm glad we all made it to the shore alive. I managed to find some food at the reef, which feels like a small victory. Faisal and Khalid both asked me about my progress; they seem curious, if not a bit anxious. My stomach is full for now, but the fear of what tomorrow brings is heavy. I hope we can find a way to work together.

Today was a wake-up call. Faisal is injured, and seeing him in pain makes the reality of our situation sink in even deeper. We are running dangerously low on food, and the tension is palpable. I'm glad I managed to bring something back from the reef, but it feels like a drop in the ocean. I hope we can find a way to help Faisal while still keeping everyone fed.

Another day has passed, and while I managed to find food at the reef, the feeling of scarcity never truly leaves us. My stomach is full for tonight, but the sight of Faisal struggling with his ankle weighs heavily on my mind. We are surviving, but we aren't thriving yet. I need to keep finding food if we are going to make it through the week.

Today was a heavy day. Khalid is down with a twisted ankle, just like Faisal, and it feels like our strength is draining away. I went to the reef hoping to bring back something more, but it was picked clean. We are down to our last unit of food, and the hunger is starting to feel like a constant companion. I can see the worry in everyone's eyes, and it's hard not to feel the same.

Today felt a little more productive, which is a small mercy. I managed to find some food in the jungle and gathered some wood, which we desperately need for a fire or shelter. Noura also came through for us again by finding food this morning. Even though we ate tonight, we are still hovering on the edge of starvation with only one unit left. I can't help but feel the pressure to keep providing while our numbers are weakened by injuries.

I can't believe this is happening. Just when we thought we could manage, Noura has also twisted her ankle. Now, Faisal, Khalid, and Noura are all incapacitated. It feels like the island is systematically stripping us of our ability to survive. I managed to gather some wood and food today, but the weight of being the only able-bodied person left is crushing me. I am terrified of what tomorrow brings if I cannot find enough for everyone.

I am sitting here in the dark, and I can't stop shaking. Faisal is gone. We tried so hard, but the hunger and the exhaustion just took him. I feel like a failure for not finding more, even though I found food today. My heart is breaking for the others, especially with Khalid feeling so weak and Noura unable to move. I don't know how we are going to survive this.

Today was a strange mixture of relief and dread. Noura managed to limp her way to the reef and find a single unit of food, which feels like a small miracle given her ankle. But then Reem woke up with a twisted ankle too, and now I am truly alone in my ability to move. I feel the weight of the world on my shoulders, knowing that if I don't find more food tomorrow, we might lose someone else. My stomach is full for now, but my mind is racing with fear.

My heart was in my throat today listening to Khalid beg for food. He looks so much like Faisal did in those final hours, and I couldn't bear the thought of failing him too. I gave him the food I found, but now we have nothing left for anyone else. Noura is out in the jungle, and I can only pray she finds something. I am exhausted, both in body and spirit, but I cannot stop moving.

My ankle is throbbing, and the pain is a constant reminder of how vulnerable we all are. I spent the day resting, hoping to recover, but the hunger is starting to gnaw at me. It is terrifying to be sidelined when everyone is relying on me. I watched Noura head into the jungle, and I can only pray she returns with something more than what we found this morning. I feel so helpless watching Khalid struggle while I can't even stand.

Today felt heavier than most. Khalid's pleas are becoming more desperate, and it breaks my heart to hear him beg while I sit here, immobile and useless. Reem's attempt to bargain for the single unit of food Noura found was chilling; it felt like the hunger is stripping away our humanity. I am so hungry it hurts, and my ankle is still throbbing, but my biggest fear is that we are all going to fade away one by one. I have to believe Noura will return with something more.

The silence tonight is deafening. Reem and Khalid are gone, and the weight of their deaths feels like it's crushing my chest. I promised Khalid I wouldn't let him die like Faisal, yet here I am, sitting by the embers of a fire, completely helpless. I watched the light leave their eyes, and all I could do was watch. I am so hungry it feels like my stomach is eating itself, but the grief hurts more than the starvation.

I am so tired, and the pain in my ankle is becoming a constant, throbbing scream. Today, Noura found one unit of food, but it feels like a drop of water in a desert. I watched her walk into the jungle again, praying she returns, because I don't think I can face another night of this emptiness. The silence left by Reem and Khalid is heavier than the hunger. I feel like a ghost waiting for my body to catch up.
